editorial.headline: Professional Expertise, Broadly Applied
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 74999 covers a wide field of client-facing professional, scientific and technical services, open nationally to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 74999 is the broad professional-services category for work that calls on specialist professional, scientific or technical skill, usually delivered to commercial clients. Its scope is deliberately wide: it can encompass business brokerage for small and medium-sized businesses and professional practices; valuations of antiques, jewellery and similar items outside real estate and insurance; freight-bill and tariff-information audits; security, workplace-safety, agronomy, environmental and energy-saving advice; and other technical consultancy. It also reaches construction economics, non-architectural, non-engineering and non-management consultancy, and the development of technical standards used as references for testing and analysis.

The activity is equally attentive to specialist representation and advisory work. It includes agents and agencies acting for individuals in connection with films, theatre, entertainment, sport, books, games, artworks and photography, placing those works or people with publishers, producers and others. Supervisory-board activity is also within the stated scope. The common thread is not a single industry but the provision of defined expertise or representation: a business should be able to identify its actual service clearly within that wide perimeter, rather than treating the category as a substitute for an ongoing routine operation.

Registration is open at every listed scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. In practical terms, the record permits full foreign ownership for this activity at the national level. That is the central ownership position; it does not need to be softened by conditions that do not appear in the record.

Bali does not reverse that position for this code. The province-wide PMA moratorium blocks low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities, island-wide and permanently, but this activity is not blocked by that moratorium. At the Besar scale, its OSS risk is recorded as Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. Bali’s status is therefore OK or higher risk: the activity remains outside the moratorium’s blocked category, while the applicable large-scale risk classification should be treated as part of the registration picture.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali does not block this activity for PMA registration because it falls outside the province-wide moratorium’s low- and medium-low-risk category.
